storyboard.title: The Silk Road: Trade, Ideas, and a Lasting Legacy

scenes.narration: A single network once stitched continents together across deserts and mountains.
scenes.heading: The Silk Road
scenes.subheading: Stitching continents across deserts and mountains

scenes.narration: The Silk Road stretched about 7,000 kilometers, linking most lands of Asia and Europe.
It included both land routes starting in Chang'an and maritime routes spreading from the South China Sea.
During the Tang Dynasty, trade boomed and silk production hit a golden age. Merchants moved silk, porcelain, and spices like pepper and cinnamon westward.
lines: Tang Dynasty golden age for silk.
Goods moved west from China and India.

scenes.narration: But the roads carried more than goods; they moved ideas and technology too. Paper money, printing, and gunpowder traveled from China to Europe.
Religions such as Buddhism, Islam, and Christianity spread alongside traders. Buddhism moved from India into Central Asia and China through these networks.
Papermaking technology reached the Arab world and then Europe, changing record-keeping forever.
lines: to the Arab world then Europe

scenes.narration: The network also spread disease; the Black Death rode these routes to kill millions in Europe and Asia.
By the 16th century, dried-up rivers, political fragmentation, and new sea lanes caused the old routes to fade.
lines: Silk Road decline starts in 16th century
New sea lanes divert trade away

scenes.narration: Today, UNESCO protects key corridors as World Heritage sites, and China's Belt and Road Initiative revives the spirit of connection.

facts.text: The Silk Road stretches about 7,000 kilometers.
facts.quote: The Silk Road stretches about 7,000 kilometers, connecting most lands of Asia and Europe.

facts.text: It connects most lands of Asia and Europe.
facts.quote: The Silk Road stretches about 7,000 kilometers, connecting most lands of Asia and Europe.

facts.text: The Silk Road includes land routes and maritime routes.
facts.quote: Generally, the silk roads include the land silk routes and maritime silk routes.

facts.text: The land Silk Road began in China's Chang'an.
facts.quote: The silk road (the land silk road) was a vast network of trade routes that spanned the entire continent of Asia from China's Chang'an

facts.text: The maritime Silk Road spread from the South China Sea.
facts.quote: The maritime silk road spreads outward from the South China Sea

facts.text: The Silk Road network has several main routes with many branches.
facts.quote: It is not easy to "follow" the Silk Road on the map, because there are several main routes that also have many branches.

facts.text: The Tang Dynasty (618–907 CE) expanded many trade routes, making it a golden age for the Silk Road.
facts.quote: Because of its expansion of many trade routes that welcomed a lot of merchants and travelers from far routes, the Tang Dynasty can be described as a

facts.text: The Tang capital Chang'an is now called Xi'an.
facts.quote: The capital of the dynasty is Chang'an, which is now known as Xi'an.

facts.text: The Han Dynasty is credited with the discovery and production of silk.
facts.quote: The Han Dynasty was credited with the discovery and production of silk.

facts.text: The Tang Dynasty was the golden age of silk production and trade in China and along the Silk Road.
facts.quote: The Tang Dynasty was the golden age of silk production and trade in China and along the Silk Road.

facts.text: The Byzantine Empire was a significant site for Chinese silk.
facts.quote: The Byzantine Empire was a significant site for Chinese silk.

facts.text: Silk connected the Han Dynasty, Tang Dynasty, and Byzantine Empire as trading partners.
facts.quote: All three dynasties are connected and intertwined with silk and its significance and trade along the Silk Road.

facts.text: The Silk Road carried many valuable commodities westward, including silk and porcelain from China.
facts.quote: silk and porcelain from China; pepper, batik, spices, perfumes, glass beads, gems and muslin from India

facts.text: Spices such as pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg came from India and the East Indies.
facts.quote: pepper, batik, spices, perfumes, glass beads, gems and muslin from India; incense, cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg from the East Indies

facts.text: The Silk Road transmitted ideas, technology, and culture in addition to trade goods.
facts.quote: The Silk Road was a conduit for ideas, technology and culture as well as trade.

facts.text: Innovations introduced to Europe from China included paper money, printing, and gunpowder.
facts.quote: Innovations introduced to Europe from China included playing cards, porcelain, art motifs, styles of furniture, paper money, printing and gunpowder.

facts.text: Maritime trade routes known as the Spice Roads stretched over 15,000 kilometers from Japan to the Mediterranean.
facts.quote: stretched over 15,000 kilometers, from the west coast of Japan, past the Chinese coast, through South East Asia, and past India to reach the Middle East and so to the Mediterranean

facts.text: Around the 1st century AD, 36 languages were spoken in the markets of major Central Asian cities.
facts.quote: It is said that in the A.D. 1st century 36 languages were spoken in the markets of the major Central Asian cities.

facts.text: The Silk Road facilitated the exchange of goods, ideas, religions, and technologies between East and West, fostering cross-cultural interactions.
facts.quote: The Silk Road facilitated the exchange of goods, ideas, religions, and technologies between East and West, fostering cross-cultural interactions.

facts.text: Buddhism spread from India into Central Asia, China, and beyond via the Silk Roads.
facts.quote: One of the most profound cultural exchanges facilitated by the Silk Roads was the spread of Buddhism from India into Central Asia, China, and beyond.

facts.text: Major religions like Buddhism, Zoroastrianism, Islam, and Christianity travelled along with traders, influencing local cultures.
facts.quote: Major religions like Buddhism, Zoroastrianism, Islam, and Christianity travelled along with traders, influencing local cultures and promoting mutual understanding between different civilizations.

facts.text: Papermaking technology spread from China to the Arab world and then to Europe via the Silk Road.
facts.quote: The Silk Road was vital in spreading papermaking technology from China to the Arab world, and eventually to Europe.

facts.text: Chinese paper and papermaking technology introduced to the Islamic world during the 8th century revolutionised record-keeping, education, and literature.
facts.quote: the introduction of paper and papermaking technology by the Chinese to the Islamic world during the 8th century revolutionised record-keeping, education, and literature.

facts.text: Scientific knowledge and technological innovations such as the compass, papermaking, and printing techniques were exchanged.
facts.quote: The exchange of scientific knowledge and technological innovations. The compass, papermaking, and printing techniques are notable examples.

facts.text: The Ottoman Empire competed for control of overland trade routes starting in 1453, pushing Europeans to find sea alternatives.
facts.quote: From 1453 onwards, the Ottoman Empire began competing with other gunpowder empires for greater control over the overland routes, which prompted European polities to seek alternatives

facts.text: This Ottoman competition marked the start of the Age of Discovery and European colonialism.
facts.quote: This marked the beginning of the Age of Discovery, European colonialism, and the further intensification of globalization.

facts.text: Modern projects like the Eurasian Land Bridge and China's Belt and Road Initiative are called the New Silk Road.
facts.quote: the name "New Silk Road" is used to describe several large infrastructure projects along many of the historic trade routes; among the best known are the Eurasian Land Bridge and the Chinese Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)

facts.text: UNESCO made the Chang'an-Tianshan corridor a World Heritage Site in 2014.
facts.quote: UNESCO designated the Chang'an-Tianshan corridor of the Silk Road as a World Heritage Site in 2014

facts.text: UNESCO added the Zarafshan-Karakum Corridor as a World Heritage Site in 2023.
facts.quote: and the Zarafshan-Karakum Corridor in 2023.

facts.text: The Mongol Empire's fragmentation ended the Silk Road's political and economic unity.
facts.quote: The fragmentation of the Mongol Empire loosened the political, cultural, and economic unity of the Silk Road.

facts.text: The Silk Road historically transported goods such as silk, porcelain, pepper, and spices to countries along the routes.
facts.quote: the land and maritime silk roads have brought silk, porcelain, pepper, spices to countries along the routes

facts.text: The Silk Road enabled communication and learning in commodities, technologies, personnel, and ideas between countries.
facts.quote: enable countries along the roads to communicate and learn from each other in terms of commodities, technologies, personnel and ideas

facts.text: The Silk Road promoted economic, cultural, and social development of relevant countries.
facts.quote: promote economic, cultural and social development of relevant countries

facts.text: The Silk Road facilitated harmonious co-existence and common development of various races, religions, and cultures.
facts.quote: facilitate harmonious co-existence and common development of various races, religions and cultures

facts.text: The most precious spiritual heritage of the Silk Road is the idea of peaceful cooperation, openness, inclusiveness, mutual learning, and win-win results.
facts.quote: The most precious spiritual heritage that silk road has left with us is the idea of peaceful cooperation, openness and inclusiveness, mutual learning and win-win results

facts.text: The Belt and Road Initiative inherits and carries forward the Silk Road spirit with oriental wisdom like 'harmony with differences' and 'inclusiveness'.
facts.quote: The Belt and Road Initiative inherits and carries forward the Silk Road spirit with oriental wisdom such as "harmony with differences" and "inclusiveness"

facts.text: The Silk Road was a network of paths connecting China with the Mediterranean across deserts and mountains.
facts.quote: an intricate network of paths that crossed relentless deserts and icy mountains to connect China with the Mediterranean

facts.text: The decline of the Silk Road began roughly in the 16th century.
facts.quote: which occurred roughly beginning in the 16th century

facts.text: Scientists found that rivers in the Taklamakan Desert and Tarim Basin dried up, contributing to the Silk Road's decline.
facts.quote: the water that flowed —or stopped flowing— through the rivers of the Taklamakan Desert, in the Tarim Basin (northwestern China)

facts.text: When rivers dried up, people left or died, and remaining oasis states fought over water, reducing their ability to sustain long-distance trade.
facts.quote: People left or died when the rivers dried up. And those who remained were trapped in fierce competition for water. A high frequency of conflicts among oasis states may have reduced their resilience to sustain long-distance trade

facts.text: Researchers say hydrological change was not the only cause but interacted with political, economic, and military factors.
facts.quote: all these factors —political, economic, military— interacted with a backdrop that had never been quantified until now: available water

facts.text: Other factors included Mongol conquests destroying cities and irrigation, maritime routes diverting trade after 1550 CE, Timur-China hostilities, and a shift to nomadic pastoralism over irrigated agriculture.
facts.quote: The Mongol conquests of the 13th century depopulated cities and destroyed irrigation systems. The rise of the maritime route, evidenced by shipwrecked ceramics from 1550 CE onward, diverted trade to the oceans. Hostilities between Timur and China in the early 15th century reduced trade for years. The increase of nomadic pastoralism versus small-scale irrigated agriculture may have reduced stable urban markets

facts.text: The Silk Road was a network of land and sea trade routes connecting China and the Far East with Europe from 130 B.C. to A.D. 1453.
facts.quote: The Silk Road, a network of land and sea trade routes that connected China and the Far East with Europe from 130 B.C. to A.D. 1453

facts.text: The Silk Road facilitated the exchange of goods like fabric, leather, spices, precious stones, and innovations such as paper-making and printing technology.
facts.quote: became a vital source for everything from fabric and leather goods to spices and precious stones. It connected communities and allowed them to share innovations such as paper-making and printing technology

facts.text: The Silk Road enabled the Black Death to spread from Central Asia to Europe, creating one of the first great pandemics.
facts.quote: It enabled one of the first great pandemics—the plague known as the Black Death—to spread along its route and eventually reach the edge of Europe

facts.text: The Black Death killed more than 50 million people in Europe between 1346 and 1352.
facts.quote: where it killed more than 50 million people between 1346 and 1352.

facts.text: The Silk Road allowed sustained transmission of diseases endemic to Central Asia to move along the route to Europe.
facts.quote: The Silk Road allowed, possibly for the first, the sustained transmission of diseases endemic to Central Asia to move out along the Road to Europe

facts.text: The Black Death killed an estimated 25 million people in Asia and North Africa between 1347 and 1350.
facts.quote: It's estimated that the Black Death killed 25 million people in Asia and North Africa between 1347 and 1350

facts.text: The Belt and Road Initiative is a global infrastructure and economic development strategy launched by the government of China in 2013.
facts.quote: global infrastructure and economic development strategy of the government of China since 2013

facts.text: The historic routes include the land paths used by Marco Polo and Ibn Battuta and the maritime routes of Ming admiral Zheng He.
facts.quote: Marco Polo and Ibn Battuta's routes in the north and the maritime expedition routes of Ming dynasty admiral Zheng He in the south

facts.text: Projects under the initiative include ports, railways, highways, power stations, aviation, and telecommunications across over 150 countries.
facts.quote: Projects in over 150 countries include ports, railways, highways, power stations, aviation, and telecommunications

facts.text: As of 2017, the initiative covered more than 68 countries representing 65% of the world population and 40% of global GDP.
facts.quote: covering more than 68 countries, including 65% of the world population and 40% of the global gross domestic product as of 2017
